questions.question: If the simple interest on a sum of money for 5 years at 10% per annum is Rs. 900, what is the compound interest on the same at the same rate and for the 2 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time = 5years

Rate of Interest = 10%

Simple Interest = 900

**Formula:**

SI = PRT/100

Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

CI = Amount – Sum

Here, P = Principal, R = Rate, CI = Compound interest, n and t = Time

**Calculation:**

Sum = (900 × 100)/5 × 10

⇒ 1800

Amount = 1800 × [1 + (10/100])²

⇒ 1800 × 11/10 × 11/10

⇒ 2178

CI = Amount – Sum

⇒ 2178 – 1800

⇒ Rs. 378

**∴ The compound interest on the same sum is Rs. 378.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bbdcd63830cc8c1e3aeeb14ed3c92a36c0ae740124f7b06e8ba0ef14a6e4910.png] 

Amount = (900 × 100)/5 × 10 × 11/10 × 11/10 = 2178

Compound interest = 2178 - 1800 = Rs. 378

∴ The compound interest on the same sum is Rs. 378.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest, when interest is compounded 5-monthly, and the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 12,000 for 1{ 1 over 4} years at 12% per annum?
questions.solution:

Principal = Rs. 12,000

Time = 1{ 1 over 4} years = 5/4 

Rate = 12% 

Condition for C.I. = 5-monthly compound interest

Condition for S.I. = yearly

**Concept used:**

Condition = 5-monthly compound interest

New Time = Time × 12/5

New Rate = Rate ÷ 12/5

Effective rate for S.I. = Rate × Time 

**Calculations:**

New time = (5/4) × 12/5 = 3 years

New rate = 12% × 5/12 = 5%

For 1st two durations = 5 + 5 + 25/100 = 10.25%

For next 3rd duration = 10.25 + 5 + (10.25 × 5)/100 = 15.7625%

Effective rate for S.I. = 12 × 5/4 = 15%

Difference between CI – SI = (15.7625 – 15) × 12000 = 0.7625 × 12000 = Rs.91.50

questions.question: Find the difference between CI & SI for 2 years at 8% rate of interest. If the principal is 625 rupee.
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The principal is 625 rupee

Rate is 8%

**Concept: **

SI = (P × R × T)/100

CI = P[(1 + r/100)ⁿ - 1]

Here, n is the number of terms in the year.

**Calculation: **

The simple interest for 2 years

⇒ (625 × 8 × 2)/100

⇒ 25 × 2 × 2

⇒ 100 rupee

Now, Compound interest for 2 years is 

⇒ 625[(1 + 8/100)² - 1]

⇒ 625[(108/100)² - 1]

⇒ 625[(108)² - (100)²] × 1/10000

⇒ (208 × 8)/16

⇒ 104 rupee

Now, The difference between CI and SI is

⇒ 104 - 100

⇒ 4

**∴ The difference between CI and SI is 4. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6bd67c9563cdde4a0dfe99b7686282bc07365f691adfb64c907de66aebe4b011.png] 

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is P(r/100)²

The difference is 

⇒ 625(8/100)²

⇒ 625 × 4/625

⇒ 4

**∴ The difference between CI and SI is 4. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

questions.question: The difference between simple and compound interest on Rs. 1,000 for 3 years at 5% p.a. interest is:
questions.solution:
∵ Simple interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

⇒ Simple interest = (1000 × 5 × 3)/100 = Rs. 150

Also,

When the interest is compounded annually,

Compound interest = Principal × [(1 + Rate/100)Time – 1]

⇒ Compound Interest = 1000 × [(1 + 5/100)³ – 1] = 1000 × 0.1576 = Rs. 157.6

∴ Required difference = 157.6 – 150 = Rs. 7.6

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum deposited at 8% p.a. for 8 years is Rs. 16,000. What will be the compound interest on the same sum at one fourth of the above rate of interest for 2 years?
questions.solution:
**Given**:

The simple interest on a sum deposited at 8% p.a. for 8 years is Rs. 16,000. 

**Formula Used**:

Compound interest = Principal × [(1 + rate/100)ⁿ - 1]; n = time period

Simple interest = (Principal × time × rate)/100

**Calculation**:

Let the principal sum be Rs. 'x'

⇒ 16000 = x × 8 × 8/100

⇒ x = Rs. 25000 

For compound interest, rate of interest = 8/4 = 2% p.a 

⇒ required Compound interest = 25000 × [(1 + 2/100)² - 1] = 1010

∴ required C.I = Rs. 1010

questions.question: The Compound Interest on a certain sum for 2 years at a fixed annual rate is ₹3090, and the Simple Interest on the same sum for 3 years at the same rate is ₹4500. Find the total amount after getting the interest.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Principal on CI = 3090

Time for CI = 2 years

Principal on SI = 4500

Time for SI = 3 years

**FORMULAE USED:**

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**CALCULATION:**

Simple Interest = 4500 (three years)

Simple Interest = 1500 (one year)

Compound Interest = 1500 (1st year)

Compound Interest = 1590 (2nd year)

Rate = (90 / 1500) × 100

Rate = 6%

Simple Interest = 6 × 3 = 18% (three years)

⇒ 18% = 4500

⇒ 1% = 250

⇒ 100% = 25000

Amount = 25000 + 4500 = 29500 (Including SI)

Amount = 25000 + 3090 = 28090 (including CI)

Total amount = 57590

∴ The required value is Rs. 57590

questions.question: If the difference of SI and CI for 2 years on an amount of rupees Rs. 1500 is Rs.150. Find rate%.
questions.solution:
**Given**

SI - CI = 150

Principal = Rs.1500

**Formula used**

(SI - CI) for 2 years = P(R / 100)²

P = Principal

R = Rate

**Calculation**

SI - CI = 6000( R / 100)²

⇒ 150 = 1500(R / 100)²

⇒ 1 / 10 = (R / 100)²

⇒ R² = 10000 / 10

⇒ R = 10√ 10

**∴ Rate is (10√ 10)%**

questions.question: On a certain sum of money, the compound interest for 2 years is Rs. 304.5 and the simple interest for the same period of time is Rs. 290. The rate of interest per annum:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

C.I for 2 years = Rs. 304.5

S.I for 2 years = Rs. 290

**Calculation:**

S.I for 1 year = Rs. (290/2) = Rs. 145

Difference between S.I and C.I = Rs. (304.5 – 290)

⇒ Rs. 14.5

Rate of interest per annum = (14.5/145) × 100%

⇒ 10%

**∴ The rate of interest per annum is 10%**
